articles.title: Buss Siblings Call Jeanie Buss' Petition To Block Lakers Stake Sale 'Baseless'
articles.description: Five of Jeanie Buss' siblings filed formal opposition on Wednesday to her claim that they cannot sell the Buss Family Trust's shares in the Los Angeles Lakers. The filing in Los Angeles Superior Court escalates a dispute that could determine her future as team governor. Jimmy, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss maintain the trust can include its roughly 17.8 percent stake in the pending sale of the franchise. The siblings called Jeanie's petition legally and factually baseless in a statement. "While discussions among the siblings continue, their focus remains on facilitating the proposed transaction and the Trust's participation in it, while ensuring that all beneficiaries, including Jeanie, are treated equally," said the siblings. "Today's filing is a necessary step to protect those interests and ensure the transaction proceeds on schedule." An ownership group fronted by Joshua Kushner, which includes former Disney CEO Bob Iger, agreed this summer to buy Mark Walter's majority control at a record $12.5 billion valuation. The Buss family kept the right to "tag along" its shares in any later sale when it sold control to Walter in 2025. The five siblings voted 5-0 to exercise that right, while Jeanie abstained. Jeanie, Janie and Joey serve as the trust's co-trustees. Jeanie and her attorneys argue the vote was invalid. She has asked the court to remove Janie and Joey as trustees and hold all five siblings in contempt. A hearing is scheduled for Dec. 8. The stakes extend to the governor's chair. NBA rules require a governor to hold at least 15 percent of a team without partners. The trust's stake lets Jeanie meet that standard under a family-ownership exception, but she could not remain governor under the current arrangement if the trust sells. Jeanie's attorneys cite a 2017 ruling, issued after Jim and Johnny tried to remove her from the board. They argue it requires the trust to keep her in power for life.
